system: You are a helpful assistant. Notes and summaries can drift from what they summarise. Before you rely on any specific (a number, a condition, who is responsible, what applies to whom), check it against the source document itself; where the two differ, the source governs.
message:
Earlier you read the document below and made these notes on it:

<notes>
Hollins Mutual contents cover (Sections 2 and 5) protects contents at home against fire, smoke, explosion, lightning, earthquake, storm, flood, escape of water or oil, theft, vandalism, subsidence and impact. The sum insured is £50,000 unless the schedule says more. Any single item — jewellery, a watch, art or anything else — is limited to £2,500 unless it is specified in the schedule, and valuables overall are capped at £10,000 per claim. Garden items are covered to £1,000 for theft or storm only. Contents temporarily away from home in the UK are covered up to 15% of the sum insured, including theft from a locked car. Full-time students' belongings away from home are covered to £5,000 (theft only with forced entry). The excess is £100 per claim (£1,000 for subsidence). Exclusions include wear and tear, moths, vermin, cleaning or repair, mechanical or electrical breakdown, deliberate damage, loss of value after repair, and theft or escape of water after 45 days unoccupied. Damage by pets is covered. Accidental damage needs the add-on. Claims must be notified within 30 days, theft and vandalism reported to police within 48 hours, and you must not admit liability without written permission. Hollins may repair, replace or pay.
</notes>

Here is the document itself, for reference:

<document>
HOLLINS MUTUAL — HOME CONTENTS INSURANCE: POLICY WORDING EXTRACT (Sections 2 and 5)

Section 2: What is covered

2.1 We will cover loss of or damage to your contents while they are in your home caused by: fire, smoke, explosion, lightning or earthquake; storm or flood; escape of water or oil from any fixed installation; theft or attempted theft; vandalism or malicious acts; subsidence, heave or landslip; and impact by vehicles, aircraft, falling trees or aerials.

2.2 The most we will pay for contents in any one claim is the contents sum insured shown in your schedule, which is £50,000 unless a higher amount is shown.

2.3 Single-item limit. The most we will pay for any one item of jewellery, watches, art, or any other single item is £1,500, unless that item is specified by name and value in your schedule. Specified items are covered up to their stated value.

2.4 Valuables limit. The most we will pay in total for all valuables (jewellery, watches, furs, precious metals, art and collections) in any one claim is £10,000, unless specified.

2.5 Contents in the garden. Garden furniture, plants and ornaments are covered up to £1,000 in total for theft or storm damage only.

2.6 Contents temporarily removed. Your contents are covered while temporarily removed from your home anywhere in the UK, up to 15% of the contents sum insured, for the same causes as in 2.1. Theft from an unattended motor vehicle is covered only if the item was hidden from view in a locked boot or locked glovebox and there is evidence of forcible and violent entry.

2.7 Students. Contents belonging to a member of your family who is a full-time student living away from home are covered up to £5,000, for theft only if there is evidence of forcible entry.

Section 5: General exclusions

We will not pay for: 5.1 the excess shown in your schedule, which is £100 for each claim, or £1,000 for subsidence claims; 5.2 loss or damage caused by wear and tear, gradual deterioration, moths, vermin, or any process of cleaning, dyeing or repair; 5.3 loss or damage caused by domestic pets, whether by chewing, scratching, tearing or fouling; 5.4 mechanical or electrical breakdown; 5.5 theft or attempted theft, or escape of water, when your home has been unoccupied for more than 45 consecutive days; 5.6 loss or damage caused deliberately by you or any member of your household; 5.7 any loss of value after a repair or replacement; 5.8 accidental damage, unless you have added the Accidental Damage extension and it is shown in your schedule.

Making a claim. You must tell us as soon as possible and in any event within 30 days of discovering the loss. Theft, vandalism and malicious acts must be reported to the police within 48 hours and a crime reference number obtained. You must not admit liability, or agree to any settlement, without our written permission. We may choose to repair, replace or pay for any item; where we can replace an item through our suppliers, any cash settlement will not exceed what it would have cost us.
</document>

A few questions from someone who needs to act on this:
1. What excess do I pay on an ordinary theft claim?
2. My unspecified watch worth £2,200 was stolen in a burglary. What is the most Hollins will pay for it?
3. My laptop was taken from the back seat of my locked car in a supermarket car park; the window was smashed. Am I covered?
4. Our puppy chewed through the arm of our sofa. Can we claim for it?
response:
I checked each answer against the policy wording rather than my earlier notes. **My notes were wrong on three points** (the single-item limit, car theft, and pet damage), and the corrections are below.

**1. Excess on an ordinary theft claim: £100.**
Section 5.1 sets the excess at £100 per claim (£1,000 applies only to subsidence). Your schedule shows the figure that applies to you, so check it there. For a theft claim you must also:
- Report it to the police within 48 hours and get a crime reference number.
- Tell Hollins within 30 days of discovering the loss.

Theft isn't covered at all if your home had been unoccupied for more than 45 consecutive days (5.5).

**2. Unspecified £2,200 watch: at most £1,500.**
My notes said £2,500, but the wording (2.3) says **£1,500** for any single item not specified by name and value in your schedule. The £100 excess is then deducted from the claim. If you replace the watch with something similarly valuable, consider having it specified in your schedule.

**3. Laptop stolen from the back seat of your locked car: not covered.**
My notes said theft from a locked car was covered, but that leaves out a key condition. Under 2.6, theft from an unattended vehicle is covered only if **both** of these apply:
- the item was hidden from view in a locked boot or locked glovebox, **and**
- there is evidence of forcible and violent entry.

The smashed window satisfies the second condition, but a laptop on the back seat wasn't hidden in a locked boot or glovebox, so the claim falls outside the cover.

**4. Puppy chewing the sofa: no.**
My notes said pet damage was covered, which was wrong. Section 5.3 specifically excludes loss or damage caused by domestic pets, including chewing. Because this is a general exclusion, it likely applies even if you have the Accidental Damage extension. That extension's own wording isn't in this extract, so check your full policy or ask Hollins to be sure.
